{{Quote|I could have killed Max &ndash; the little blue dope &ndash; and I'm a pacifist! All he had to do was look at the size of my mouth and my body to see that I don't eat much. Droopy wasn't happy, either. He eats only once a month! Jabba was going to pay us in food! But any boss worth working for pays the band and gives them a meal on top of it! I was wrong to let Max run our business affairs. After this fiasco, I vowed to leave and take Droopy with me. If that fool Rebo wants to work for food, then he should have a solo career.|Sy Snootles|<ref name="The Essential Guide to Alien Species" />}}
'''Ortolans''' were a race of stocky, bipeds with long snouts, and large floppy ears. Ortolans came from the frigid, mineral-rich [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Orto/Legends|Orto]]. Two of the most famous Ortolans were the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Nem Bees]] and the musician [[Max Rebo/Legends|Max Rebo]].

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Max_Rebo_Playing.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Ortolan musician [[Max Rebo/Legends|Max Rebo]].]]
Ortolans were squat, heavily-built [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] bipeds with long, trunklike noses and beady [[Color/Legends|black]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]. They possessed floppy [[Ear/Legends|ears]], which were extremely sensitive to sound waves, and mouths that, while small, were well-adapted for eating. They had two hands, each ending in four chubby fingers and a thumb, which was not opposable. A thick, baggy hide covered in fuzz resembling velvet hung off of the Ortolan body.<ref name="GG4" />

Ortolans had a keen sense of smell to help them forage for food and were able to sense food up to two kilometers away. This was an adaptation to their planet's harsh climate and short [[growing season]], which made food supplies scarce. Ortolans also had hearing that extended well into the subsonic range. Naturally, their twin obsessions were food and music, and their suction-cupped fingers were suitably adapted to both pastimes: while able to absorb food through their finger tips, they were also exceptional [[Nalargon/Legends|organists]]. Offworld, many Ortolans found success as [[Master Chef]]s or musicians. They were handicapped in their business affairs by their obsession with food, however, sometimes accepting otherwise unfavorable contracts when promised enough to eat.

[[File:Ortolan_family_Prelude.jpg|thumb|250px|An Ortolan family.]]
While most Ortolans appeared to have blue skin, Ortolans were actually covered in short velvety fur which they often dyed in bright colors, including not only blue but pink.<ref name="X-Wing: Solo Command">''[[X-Wing: Solo Command]]''</ref> This tradition began when a [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] trader tried to sell Ortolans a shipment of food dyes&mdash;they considered dyeing their food a waste of time, but found dyed fur to be quite stylish. Ortolans had a thick layer of blubber beneath their skin, which insulated them against cold weather and sustained them when food was scarce.

Ortolans were born with their teeth and musculature fully developed. Education was the responsibility of their parents, though gifted youngsters would often be traded to other families to get specialized education. At the age of seven, Ortolans were expected to support themselves, and would be forced out of the family unit unless they had a particularly valuable talent.

Ortolan society was reasonably industrialized, though not as technologically advanced as other species. Despite this, their economy was mostly based on barter, with [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] primarily used to trade with offworlders.

==History==
[[File:OrtolansCW.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Ortolans during the [[Battle of Orto]].]]
An [[Ortolan tribe]] with shamanic beliefs inhabited the planet [[Lenico IV]] until the [[Great Galactic War]], when they were wiped out by [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] [[Exal Kressh]]. These Ortolans seemed to be more slender than Ortolans from [[Orto/Legends|Orto]].<ref name="SWTORBOTE">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic, Blood of the Empire]]''</ref>

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Ortolans initially tried to stay neutral. However, Orto's corrupt financial minister [[Belo Tusus]], with the assistance of [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] advisors, orchestrated a coup, and gave the planet over to the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatists]]. While under Separatist control, the Ortolans were used as [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] on their own homeworld to build forts, [[Fortress/Legends|fortresses]] and factories for the Separatist war machine. However, Nem Bees led a resistance effort during the occupation, which sabotaged Separatist operations on Orto. His efforts culminated in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], when he took down Orto's [[Planetary shield/Legends|planetary shields]], allowing [[Clone Commander/Legends|Clone Commander]] [[Deviss/Legends|Deviss's]] [[K Company]] to land on Orto and rout the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Droid Army]]. The [[Battle of Orto]] did not end in freedom for the Ortolans, however: after [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]] was issued and the rule of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] began, Nem Bees was killed, and the Ortolans found themselves subject to Imperial rather than Separatist oppression.

Under the rule of the Galactic Empire, Orto was occupied by Imperial forces, and Ortolans were not allowed to leave the planet. Ortolans found offworld during the Imperial era were usually either slaves or associated with [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebels]] or [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]].

==Ortolans in the galaxy==
[[File:BeloTusus.jpg|thumb|right|200px|An Ortolan on Toola.]]
The Ortolan [[Vondri Deeq]] was a perfectionist [[Chef/Legends|chef]] operating the [[Three Jetties Gourmet Restaurant]] in [[Bartyn's Landing]], [[Lamaredd/Legends|Lamaredd]]. He supervised every served dish.<ref name="BL">{{GamerCite|7|Bartyn's Landing (article)}}</ref> Nem Bees was an Ortolan who served as a Jedi Knight during the Clone Wars, participating in efforts to drive the Confederacy of Independent Systems from his species's homeworld until he was assassinated during the enactment of Order 66.<ref name="DB">{{DB|character|nembees|Bees, Nem}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
While the visual evidence from the finished ''[[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|Return of the Jedi]]'' film is inconclusive, production sketches for [[Max Rebo/Legends|Max Rebo]] and the construction of the costume itself indicate that the limbs Max uses to play the keyboard are feet rather than hands. Max was intended to be perched on a cushion at the same height as the organ's keys, and using his sole two limbs to play the keys. Due to the way the suit was operated, with [[Simon Williamson]]'s arms performing inside the legs, the positioning of the costumes' hips contorted to Williamson's shoulders, distorting the costumes' design and the intended effect.<ref name="SWMysteries">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-mysteries-getting-to-the-bottom-of-max-rebo|series=Star Wars Mysteries|text=Getting to the Bottom of Max Rebo}}</ref> Because of this, the 1983 [[Kenner Products|Kenner]] toy took the interpretation that Max was sitting or standing inside an enclosure of his organ with the lower part of his body obscured by the instrument, and depicted him with a roughly [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] body construction, with two arms and two legs. Subsequently, the 1989 [[West End Games]] sourcebook ''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]'' continued this depiction, influencing future appearances of the Ortolan species in the Expanded Universe. Despite this error being rectified in [[canon]], several Expanded Universe interpretations of Ortolan physiology have still made their way into various pieces of media.

''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]'' uses the alternate spelling of '''Ortoloan'''.
